title: federal reserve / fomc / christopher waller | Speech Neutral | One Transitory Shock After Another
summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller delivered a speech on April 17, 2026, outlining how the U.S. economy faces a series of supply-side shocks from both the Middle East conflict disrupting energy production and the cumulative effects of import tariffs, which together risk creating more lasting inflation similar to pandemic-era dynamics. He also detailed unprecedented changes in labor supply, with net immigration falling from 2.3 million in 2024 to approximately 400,000 in 2025 and projected near zero in 2026, fundamentally reducing the number of jobs needed to maintain stable unemployment.
